notice: This is the first-MVP vertical-slice delivery-planning model. It groups the accepted 25-story backlog into observable, independently demonstrable product/operational outcomes. It does not create, reinterpret, or resolve any story, requirement, validation gate, or technical-baseline decision, and it grants no implementation, ADR, test, task, or execution-packet authority.

slices.title: Guest builds a valid basket and submits a feasible pickup order
slices.observable_outcome: A guest customer browses the published menu, configures an informed and safe item, and submits a feasible pickup order with its resulting commitment.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The customer basket becomes a submitted order with a feasible pickup commitment, or the customer is returned to browsing/checkout with the nearest feasible alternatives.

slices.title: Customer considers a compatible basket recommendation
slices.observable_outcome: A customer with an eligible basket item views currently eligible, compatible recommendations and may add one to the basket without any automatic basket change.

VS-ORDERING-001.rationale: ST-UPSELL-001 declares no story-level dependency, so this is not an induced dependency. UC-UPSELL-001's accepted precondition is 'The customer has a basket', and only the core ordering slice's catalog/basket behavior (ST-CATALOG-001) produces an eligible basket item for the recommendation to evaluate against.

slices.acceptance_boundary: The basket changes only through the customer's confirmed acceptance of an offered recommendation, or remains unchanged if the customer ignores it or no eligible recommendation exists.

slices.title: Customer tracks an order privately and responds to a revised pickup commitment
slices.observable_outcome: A customer privately follows the material status of a submitted order and accepts or declines a proposed pickup-time revision within the configured response window.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The private tracking view reflects the current material order/pickup status, and a customer response (or its expiry) is reflected in the order's operational handling.

slices.title: Staff registers and revises assisted telephone or in-person orders
slices.observable_outcome: An authorised staff member records a telephone or in-person pickup order into the shared operational lifecycle and applies an authorised later telephone-requested change to an existing order.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The assisted order (or its authorised change) is reflected in the shared order lifecycle and kitchen queue with a feasible, revalidated pickup opportunity.

slices.title: Staff controls online ordering admission mode and resolves pending web orders
slices.observable_outcome: An authorised staff member sets the safe online-order admission mode for current conditions, and resolves any web order that mode places into manual review.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Online ordering follows the selected admission mode, and every pending web order under manual review receives a recorded accept/reject/alternative decision.

slices.title: Owner maintains normal service capacity
slices.observable_outcome: Jaime maintains the approved normal service schedule and capacity for planned service.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Future order admission reflects the current approved normal service plan.

slices.title: Staff and responsible person apply temporary current-service capacity controls
slices.observable_outcome: Authorised staff or the responsible person apply a permitted temporary current-service pickup-window adjustment or preparation delay/capacity reduction limited to the current service.

VS-CAPACITY-001.rationale: Neither ST-CAPACITY-002 nor ST-CAPACITY-003 declares a story-level dependency, so this is not an induced dependency. Both stories' accepted context adjusts an individual pickup window or capacity that already exists only because Jaime's normal service plan (ST-CAPACITY-001) established it, and BR-CAPACITY-003 binds every temporary control to that pre-existing plan without changing it.

slices.acceptance_boundary: Order admission reflects an active temporary current-service adjustment without changing the normal service plan's approved capacity or hours.

slices.title: Kitchen prepares and progresses accepted orders
slices.observable_outcome: Kitchen staff receive, acknowledge, prepare, and progress every accepted order to ready, with the customer notified once it is ready for collection.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Every accepted order's current preparation status is visible, accurate, and actionable on a real kitchen tablet through to ready/handed-over.

slices.title: Staff keeps saleability aligned with stock
slices.observable_outcome: Staff record stock and availability adjustments so that every order channel sells only currently available, sufficiently stocked configurations.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Current saleability across all channels reflects the latest recorded stock/availability adjustment.

slices.title: Responsible person maintains approved catalog content
slices.observable_outcome: The responsible person creates and maintains accurate, approved catalog content and configured product options for customer browsing.
slices.acceptance_boundary: A confirmed catalog change becomes the published, customer-visible catalog content without breaking historical order integrity.

slices.title: Staff isolates unsafe sale
slices.observable_outcome: Staff stop further sale of a product or option affected by a safety or dietary-information problem and route affected accepted orders into operational review.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The affected sale scope stops immediately and every affected accepted, undelivered order is visible for operational review.

slices.title: Staff completes payment, handover, and non-collection outcomes
slices.observable_outcome: Staff record the payment actually received and hand over a ready order, or resolve an order that remains uncollected after its confirmed pickup window through the authorised non-collection process.
slices.acceptance_boundary: A ready order reaches exactly one terminal collection-counter outcome: recorded payment and handover, or authorised non-collection handling, each separately auditable.

slices.title: Staff closes an accountable service shift
slices.observable_outcome: A current team member reviews open orders, payments, and incidents, reconciles cash, and closes the responsible operational session(s) for the shift.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The shift close is recorded with its cash comparison, required operational review, and closed responsible sessions.

slices.title: Staff resolves operational incidents and escalates decisions to Jaime
slices.observable_outcome: Staff resolve an order, contact, delay, shortage, payment, or fulfilment exception within authorised limits, or escalate it as a pending decision that stays visible until Jaime resolves it.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Every visible exception has either a recorded authorised resolution or an escalated pending-decision record, in both cases preserving its history.

slices.title: Responsible person opens accountable service
slices.observable_outcome: Jaime or an authorised delegate assumes and records service responsibility before online ordering is eligible to open.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Online ordering cannot open until a current responsibility record exists for the service period.

slices.title: Owner manages staff access and delegation
slices.observable_outcome: Jaime authorises, reviews, revokes, or changes staff operational access and delegation so that access stays current and bounded.
slices.acceptance_boundary: A staff member's actual operational access matches Jaime's most recently recorded access decision.

slices.title: Responsible person reviews controlled operational reports
slices.observable_outcome: The responsible person reviews the defined channel, peak, incident, delay, performance, value, and product-combination evidence to evaluate service performance.
slices.acceptance_boundary: The report view reflects the currently defined controlled operational and pilot evidence available for review.

slices.title: Responsible person prepares and operates a controlled pilot
slices.observable_outcome: The responsible person starts, monitors, safely pauses when required, and evaluates the controlled pilot only under its approved safeguards, producing the required evidence.
slices.acceptance_boundary: Pilot activity stays within its approved controls at every point, and the defined pilot evidence is produced for its scheduled evaluation.

recommended_delivery_order_note: recommended_delivery_order is a non-binding planning recommendation only. It sequences useful early product/risk learning against hard slice dependencies; it is not an implementation commitment, release schedule, estimate, or Owner authorisation, and an unresolved PILOT/WITHOUT_JAIME/PUBLIC_LAUNCH gate does not by itself block any slice's design.
